rows.subtopic: Reaching a toy on a shelf
rows.description: A toddler stands under a low shelf, rises on tiptoe and stretches one arm toward a stuffed elephant, grunting, then tries the other hand when the first falls short.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, rigid persistence, trial and error

rows.subtopic: Reaching a toy on a shelf
rows.description: A toddler tries jumping, tugging the shelf edge and pulling the rug under the toy, one after another, and keeps repeating whichever move makes the elephant shift even a little.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, rigid persistence

rows.subtopic: Reaching a toy on a shelf
rows.subtype: Approach: using the caregiver as a tool [Action]
rows.description: A toddler points at the shelf, looks at grandmother, says "uh, uh" and pats her hand. Her arm becomes the means of reaching, so the toddler does not need to work out the reaching.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, rigid persistence, trial and error

rows.subtopic: Reaching a toy on a shelf
rows.description: After watching an older cousin drag over a small stool and climb it, a toddler pushes the same stool to the shelf and copies the climbing motion, without yet judging whether the stool is steady.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: rigid persistence, trial and error

rows.subtopic: Reaching a toy on a shelf
rows.description: A toddler keeps stretching at the same spot for several minutes and ignores the stool close by, until tears come. Repeating one failing action leaves no room to notice other options.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, trial and error

rows.subtopic: Reaching a toy on a shelf
rows.description: Frustrated, a toddler sits down and whimpers, then looks around for mother, points at the shelf and lets her lift the toy down. The toddler switches from doing it alone to asking.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, rigid persistence, trial and error

rows.description: A toddler twists, pulls, bangs the lid on the floor and pokes at the edge of a snack box. Each action is tried for a few seconds and dropped if nothing gives.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, experiment and measure

rows.description: Having watched father twist the lid off a tiffin box, a toddler copies the twisting wrist motion on a box of raisins, though the twist goes the wrong way and the lid does not open.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: experiment and measure, trial and error

rows.subtype: Approach: using the caregiver as a tool [Action]
rows.description: A toddler holds the sealed box up to mother, says "open" and waits with hands out. The caregiver is treated as a tool that turns closed boxes into open ones.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, experiment and measure, trial and error

rows.description: Once, pressing the lid corner popped a box open. The toddler now presses the corner of every lid and box, and is puzzled when a screw-top bottle does not respond.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, experiment and measure, trial and error
